name: East Suffolk Trust Nature Fund (core grants programme)
summary: Core grants of £10,000 and up, for projects of up to five years that restore habitats and species or build community-led nature recovery in Suffolk, with a focus on East Suffolk. Starts with a rolling expression of interest.

geography.label: Suffolk, with a focus on East Suffolk

amount.note: No upper limit; projects of up to five years

reporting: A project update when half the grant is spent and a final report to release the last payment; no set format, usually under two A4 pages.

steps: Discuss eligibility first if outside East Suffolk and no clear benefit to it
Expression of interest screening and eligibility review

eligibility.rule: Standard nonprofit route: own bank account, governing document and 3 unrelated decision-makers at separate addresses
Can evidence work benefiting nature and people for the public benefit
Private landowners, companies and other applicants show public benefit and only incidental private or commercial gain
Coastal or marine projects are adjacent to the Suffolk coastline
Project is outside the applicant’s statutory activities

geography.quote: East Suffolk Trust can fund work in Suffolk or its immediate surrounding area, with a particular focus on East Suffolk.

access.quote: Full applications are by invite only, with final funding decisions aligned to our quarterly Board of Trustees meetings.

window.quote: All applicants must first submit an Expression of Interest (EOI), which we accept on a rolling basis.

amount.quote: Grants start at £10,000, with no upper limit, and can support projects lasting up to five years.

pool.quote: we are restricted in how much we award by our total annual budget (currently £1.6m per year)

co_finance_required.quote: There is no formal requirement for match or partnership funding.

consortium_required.quote: There is no formal requirement for match or partnership funding.

reporting.quote: in most cases we will require a project update when 50% of the grant has been spent, and a final project report in order to release the final 20% of funds.

effort.quote: If your EOI is successful, you will be invited to submit a full application.

All applicants must first submit an expression of Interest. These are accepted on a rolling basis, with no deadlines. Full applications are by invite only, with final funding decisions aligned to our quarterly Board of Trustees meetings. 1. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST All applications must first submit an expression of interest (EOI) via our online form.
If your project is based elsewhere in Suffolk or its immediate surrounding area, with no clear benefit for East Suffolk, you must contact us before applying to discuss eligibility
All EOIs that pass initial screening will be assessed against our eligibility criteria by one or more reviewers.
Full proposals are all decided by our board of trustees, who meet four times per year.

eligibility.quote: An organisation is fully eligible if it is a not-for-profit entity with: A bank account in the organisation’s name A governing document (e.g., constitution, articles of association, or trust deed) At least three trustees, directors, or equivalent decision-makers who are not related and do not live at the same address
To be eligible for funding, you or your organisation must be able to demonstrate evidence of work delivering for nature and people, for public benefit.

If you are a private landowner, for-profit company, or other organisation, you may be eligible to apply where you can clearly demonstrate that your proposed work will deliver public benefit for nature and people, and that any personal, private or commercial benefit is incidental.
Are coastal and marine projects in scope? Yes, provided that they are adjacent to the Suffolk coastline.

WHAT WE DO NOT FUND Activity that falls outside the Trust’s funding outcomes or geographic scope Costs incurred prior to the grant start date Grants below £10,000 Costs for individual benefit Statutory activities

after_award.quote: Your funding offer will contain details of the reporting requirements for your project.
